text:
Today we had word of the poet:

amid the lullaby of mouth organs

and with the arms of the last stars hanging down,

he halted his horse.


The women's camp clapped its hands,

seasoning the corn tortillas.

The girls bit the stems of flowers,

and the old men sealed tearful friendships

amid the libations of the deep dawn.


They carried basins of water,

and the chief prepared

to wash his chest, his head, and his beard.


The potters of the seven wives

were already caressing the damp jars.

The children of the country that does nothing

lit cigarettes as long as sticks.


And in the morning sacrifice,

lambs for everyone

turned, skewered on pikes,

over the blaze of fragrant logs.


Today we had word of the poet,

because he was asleep on horseback.

He said they carry God upon their horns

and that the night has acid roses

on the carpets of the two twilights.

translation.title: Caravan
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the poem’s surreal caravan ritual, including its deliberately strange social and sacrificial images.
